title: Rice to Onana via Messi: the week’s key moves and what could follow
trail: This week’s major transfers are summed up as new signings are mooted for Manchester City, Newcastle and West Ham
body: Deals confirmed in the last week include: Lionel Messi, Paris Saint-Germain to Inter Miami Messi’s move to the MLS side on a free transfer was confirmed last Saturday and he was unveiled in Miami on Sunday. Declan Rice, West Ham to Arsenal The long-mooted move by the England midfielder was finalised as £100m plus £5m add-ons, making him the most expensive British player. Sergio Busquets, Barcelona to Inter Miami Stalwart former Spain midfielder joins as a free agent and has reunited with his teammate at Barcelona, Messi. Kim Min-jae, Napoli to Bayern Munich South Korean central defender moves for £43m. André Onana, Internazionale to Manchester United The Cameroonian goalkeeper officially signed for £44.1m to replace David de Gea, on a five-year deal with the option of an extra year. Philipp Köhn, Red Bull Salzburg to Monaco The goalkeeper has joined the Ligue 1 team for £8.6m. Aaron Ramsey, Nice to Cardiff City The Wales captain returns on a free transfer to the club where he started his career. Abakar Sylla, Club Brugge to Strasbourg The 20-year-old centre-back has moved for £18.9m. Ângelo Gabriel, Santos to Chelsea Brazilian winger, 18, moves to England for £12.9m. Hákon Haraldsson, FC Copenhagen to Lille The 20-year-old midfielder moves to the French team for £14.6m. El Chadaille Bitshiabu, Paris Saint-Germain to RB Leipzig The France Under-19 defender has joined for £12.9m. Seko Fofana, Lens to Al-Nassr The midfielder, a French-born Ivory Coast international, joins the Saudi Arabian team for £21.5m. Benjamin Mendy, free agent to Lorient After being acquitted on charges of rape and attempted rape, the former Manchester City full-back has moved to the Ligue 1 club as a free agent. Oriol Romeu, Girona to Barcelona The Spanish midfielder joins Barcelona for £3m. Milos Kerkez, AZ to Bournemouth Hungarian left-back joins on a long-term deal for £15.5m. James Trafford, Manchester City to Burnley The goalkeeper, who played a starring role in England Under-21s winning the Euros, has moved for £15m. Marvelous Nakamba, Aston Villa to Luton Zimbabwean defensive midfielder, loaned to Luton for promotion push, has signed a three-year deal for £4m. Ethan Ampadu, Chelsea to Leeds The Wales centre-back has agreed a four-year deal for £7m after largely being on loan at other clubs since 2019. In the pipeline Transfers mooted but yet to be confirmed include: Carlos Borges, Manchester City to West Ham for about £14m. Rasmus Højlund, Atalanta to Manchester United for about £60m. Moussa Diaby, Bayer Leverkusen to Aston Villa for a club-record £51.9m. Noah Okafor, Red Bull Salzburg to Milan for £12m. Josko Gvardiol, RB Leipzig to Manchester City for about £86m. Jordan Henderson, Liverpool to Al-Ettifaq for an initial £12m. Fabinho, Liverpool to Al-Ittihad for £40m. Harvey Barnes, Leicester to Newcastle for £38m. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Chelsea to Marseille on a free transfer. Follow the latest deals in our transfer interactive and the contenders in our Rumour Mill column.
